turns.text: Today's motion is, "True love is a myth." Ben argues for it, and Alice argues against it. Each gets thirty seconds to open, then we have two and a half minutes of crossfire. I will give a ten-second cue. Finally, each gets thirty seconds for a closing statement.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: True love is usually sold as a forever feeling that makes one person uniquely meant for another. But feelings change, people change, and the promise survives mostly because we repeat it. I am not denying affection or loyalty. I am arguing that the flawless, permanent thing called true love is a story, not a fact.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You've got ten seconds.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Real couples can care deeply and still discover that their supposed destiny was ordinary compatibility. We mistake powerful hope for proof, then call the disappointment tragic rather-

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Ben is right that people change, but he treats change as proof that love was never true. A promise can be real without being flawless, and a relationship can survive disappointment. True love is not a magic guarantee against loss; it is a genuine bond built through choice, care, and honesty. Calling that bond a myth erases the reality people live.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: If love ends, that does not make the love false. It means a real thing can be temporary, and true love remains more than a fantasy.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: I believe true love never lasts forever. If your bond depends on permanence, how can its ending prove it was true rather than merely intense?

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: It does not depend on permanence; that is your premise, and I reject it. A bond can be true because people freely choose one another, not because time stops moving.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: This true love lasts forever. You cannot call an enduring feeling proof of a special essence when the same devotion can be explained by memory, habit, or hope.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Those statements fit because a perfect shared life never lasts forever, while this particular love lasts forever as a memory. A lasting memory still does not make the myth real.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I grant that memory can preserve an emotion, but you keep replacing lived commitment with a definition designed to defeat it. People choose, sacrifice, and remain faithful; that makes true love real.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: That choice also creates practical disputes: whose name goes on the lease, who keeps the furniture, and how the savings are divided when plans change? I trust written agreements more than romantic promises.

turns.speaker: MOD

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: The motion asks whether true love exists, not whether paperwork can protect people when relationships fail. Since lasting devotion can be explained without destiny, the grand idea remains a myth.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: No, lasting devotion does not need destiny, and that does not make it mythical. You are answering a stronger claim than mine: I defend real love, not magical certainty.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Your weakest point is treating sincere effort as evidence of true love itself. Effort proves that people care, but it cannot prove one exceptional force beyond ordinary human attachment.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: When one partner sits beside the other through fear, keeps a promise after resentment, and asks for nothing in return, that steady care shows love is real, not mythical.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: I grant that steady care can be noble, but nobility does not establish a unique, permanent kind of love. It shows human kindness, which is enough to explain the evidence and support my side.

turns.text: That's time. So onto round three. Round three, closing statements from each debater in turn, uninterrupted. And here to summarize his position in support of true love is a myth, Ben.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: True love may describe tenderness, loyalty, and sacrifice, but those qualities do not require a mythical force. They arise from ordinary people, changing circumstances, and stories we tell ourselves. The ideal is beautiful, but beauty is not proof.

turns.text: Ben has shown that love is not always permanent, but permanence was never my test. True love means that care, trust, and commitment are genuinely felt and freely given.
